analysis:
This PR adds only documentation: a changelog entry (changelog.d/cluster-service-follows-repair.md, lines 1-6) and a new section in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~3541-3575). No source code was supplied, so the described behavior is unverified: ClusterService.listenerChange, ensureResponder, ensureControlResponder, ensureControl and ClusterSetupLinkExchange.Responder live in files outside the patch.

The docs describe a listener re-key mechanism. Listeners check every 5 s and restart when the cable port or address changes or the pairing changes. Pairing identity compares both pins, the cluster label, the link epoch and the edge, never the edge secret. A listener stops when no pairing exists. An unreadable pairing store leaves listeners unchanged, which is fail-static and keeps the earlier pairing's key active. A new pairing from the other Mac is accepted at the next check, and an earlier-release service keeps the old behavior until restart.

Security notes for later review:
1. The cluster pairing, control-lease and setup-link boundary (the two-Mac cluster listeners) is not defined in the supplied threat model (TB-002/003/007/009/010/011/012/013 are the closest). If this is new attack surface, the model may need an entry for pairing-keyed handshake listeners, covering stale-key retention when the store is unreadable and the pairing-change window of at most 5 s.
2. The control-lease listener restarts and stops without a log line (documented). This is an auditability gap but not a regression.
3. The docs claim that dropping control state on a new own SE key matches existing behavior. That cannot be verified here.

No concrete security regression is established from documentation text alone, so findings are empty. needs_deeper_review is true because the code changes described (ClusterService listener lifecycle and pairing handshake) were not supplied and may carry the security effect.
